title: n8n AI Agent Node Explained: Tools, Memory, Cost
summary: An n8n AI Agent node connects tools to a chat model that calls them in sequence until solving the problem. You'll see how to wire one into your workflows.
body_markdown:
## Run the same agent job in Activepieces


You can rebuild the same bounded worker in Activepieces: an agent is a bounded reasoning loop with a defined set of tools, a place to stop and ask a person, and a record of what it did.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


The difference is that an Agent step sits in the same flow as your deterministic steps, so the model's judgment and your fixed rules share one engine and one run trace, rather than an agent bridged to a workflow tool by a webhook.


Open a run and you see one execution, start to finish.


### Where n8n friction shows up


It tends to arrive in three places. The first is the licence: n8n's core is under the Sustainable Use License, which matters if you plan to resell or embed workflows in a product.


The second is upkeep: self-hosting means you own the updates, the database and the queue.


Third comes the agent itself, where the node's flexibility makes it easy to wire up too many tools and leave memory and cost unbounded.


None of these is a reason to leave. If your agent runs fine in n8n with a narrow toolset, a memory choice and a spending cap, stay.


This section is for the reader who has hit one of those walls and wants to see the same job elsewhere.


### Building the workflow without approval


Because Activepieces has an MIT-licensed core, the licence question is simpler. It also has a free cloud plan that asks for no card, which means you can build the whole flow before anyone approves a budget.


You can also self-host it if the data has to stay on your own machines.


Expect the same shape as the n8n build. You start with a trigger, add an AI step that holds your instructions, then give it only the integrations the job needs.


Think of integrations as Activepieces' connectors: Gmail to read or send mail, Slack to post a message to a channel, Google Sheets to read or append rows.


There are 743 of them in the open source monorepo, roughly 60% community-contributed, and the full list is at activepieces.com/integrations, so you benefit from both official and community support.


### Keep your n8n AI agent build simple


Keep the discipline from the earlier sections. Pick one trigger. Give the AI step two or three integrations, not ten, so it's more likely to select the right one.


Put a human step before anything that sends mail or writes to a sheet, and make that message short enough that the approver reads it rather than clicking yes. Then test with a handful of real inputs before you switch it on.


Because nothing carries over from n8n, treat the old workflow as a specification, not a file. Write down its trigger, its tools and its stopping condition, and build from that list.


The free cloud plan at activepieces.com gives you 1,000 credits a month, unlimited flows and up to 5 users.
